newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran asks Germany to withdraw terrorism charges.
newsitem.headline: Iran asks Germany to withdraw terrorism charges.

text.p: Iran on Monday asked Germany to end a row with the Islamic republic by withdrawing charges by a German prosecutor that Tehran ordered the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

"We would like German leaders to take a correct and principled position, clearly...correcting the error committed by the judge," head of judiciary Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi was quoted by Tehran radio as saying.
"Until German leaders announce their official position, we are assuming this problem to have been caused by an inexperienced and error-prone prosecutor," Yazdi added.

Iran has been engaged in a war of words with its main trade partner Germany since the prosecutor last week accused Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other Tehran officials of ordering the 1992 killing of three Kurdish opposition leaders and their translator at a Berlin restaurant.
"Otherwise Germany should be ready to suffer the consequences of this great error," Yazdi said, without giving further details.

Potentially at risk are trade ties worth $1.4 billion last year and Germany's "critical dialogue" with Iran -- championed by Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel as an alternative to U.S. sanctions aimed at isolating the Islamic republic.

Tehran radio said Kinkel had assured his Iranian counterpart Ali Akbar Velayati in a telephone call on Sunday that Germany did not want bilateral ties damaged and that the court's action did not necessarily reflect the stand of the Bonn government.
"The German foreign minister's remarks, though a step in the right direction, are not sufficient," it said in a commentary.
"Therefore...practical steps should be taken to make up for the (prosecutor's) illegal utterings," the state-run radio added.
In Bonn, the foreign ministry said Kinkel explained to Velayati that the German judiciary is independent and that the government has no right to interfere in court proceedings.
